definition: Terms with exactly the same letters raised to the same powers, such as $3x^{2}$ and $-5x^{2}$; only their coefficients can differ.
Rewrite an expression in its simplest form, usually by collecting like terms so each letter and power appears only once.
Multiply out brackets by multiplying every term inside by every term outside, so $3(x + 2)$ becomes $3x + 6$.
Write an expression as a product of factors, the reverse of expanding; fully factorised means no bracket can be factorised any further, as in $6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3)$.
An expression whose highest power of the variable is $2$, such as $x^{2} - 5x + 6$.
One square subtracted from another, $a^{2} - b^{2}$, which always factorises as $(a + b)(a - b)$.
Rewriting a quadratic as a bracket squared plus a number, such as $x^{2} + 6x + 1 = (x + 3)^{2} - 8$.
